subject: Re: Deployment mode & EU data residency — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sofie Larsen <sofie.larsen@nordbank.com>, Mikael Hansen <mikael.hansen@nordbank.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 05 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode & EU data residency — follow-up and next steps

Hi Sofie / Mikael —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on the right deployment mode for NordBank: hosted API vs. dedicated capacity vs. private (VPC/on-prem).

Summary of requirements you shared:
- Primary data residency requirement: all customer PII and transaction derivatives must remain in the EU (no cross-border storage).
- Latency target: 150ms p95 for core fraud-detection calls in production across EU users.
- Volume estimate: ~40M tokens/month, occasional spikes + burst window.
- Compliance: want SOC2 evidence + optional contractual data processing addendum and KMS integration.
- Long-term preference: private VPC if we need customer-managed keys and strict network controls; open to Dedicated in the short term if can meet residency and latency SLOs.

Questions for you so we can narrow options:
1) Do you need a fully customer-managed key (HSM/KMS) from day one, or is a Redwood-managed KMS with customer key lifecycle controls acceptable initially?
2) Is the requirement that "data never leaves EU" absolute for all temporary KV/prefix caches, or is regional routing plus automatic TTL acceptable for non-persistent caches?
3) Any procurement constraints (timeline for contract review / legal)?

Next steps I propose:
- Rishi and Connor to validate EU region latency and capacity profiles and share the short matrix (attached).
- If you need customer-managed KMS and air-gapped networking, we'll scope Private (VPC/on-prem) options and a high-level runbook.
- If Redwood Dedicated meets residency and KMS requirements, we can prepare a dedicated trial environment for benchmarking.

I've attached a short deck that compares deployment modes and a spreadsheet with EU region availability and latency baselines.

Available times this week for a quick follow-up: Tue/Wed 10–12 CET or Thu 14–16 CET.

Marissa
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-deployment-options.pdf, eu-region-availability.xlsx

From: Sofie Larsen <sofie.larsen@nordbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Mikael Hansen <mikael.hansen@nordbank.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Jul 2026 08:42:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Deployment mode & EU data residency — follow-up and next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is perfect, thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- KMS: We do need customer-managed keys (HSM-backed) for production. For a short pilot, we can accept Redwood-managed keys, but production must be under our KMS/HSM.
- Data residency: The requirement is strict for persisted data (logs, embeddings derived from customer PII). For ephemeral in-memory caches (e.g., KV cache for active tokens) we can accept regionally-contained caches provided they are not persisted and TTL is short (<30m).
- Procurement: procurement and legal want to see SOC2 Type II report and an initial DPA. We expect procurement review to take 3–4 weeks.

Also, two follow-ups: can you confirm which Redwood cloud regions currently have EU-hosted Dedicated nodes and whether cross-region routing ever routes EU traffic to non-EU for capacity overflow? We need assurance there is a strict policy to avoid cross-border execution for EU-tagged customers.

We can do Thu 14 CET for a 30-min follow-up — that works for Mikael and me.

Best,
Sofie
Head of Data Privacy — NordBank
sofie.larsen@nordbank.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sofie Larsen <sofie.larsen@nordbank.com>, Mikael Hansen <mikael.hansen@nordbank.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Jul 2026 06:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode & EU data residency — follow-up and next steps

Thanks Sofie — that's helpful. Short answers inline below and a plan for Thu's call: 

- KMS: Understood. For production we'll scope Private (VPC) with customer-managed HSM/KMS. For the pilot we can use a Dedicated trial with Redwood-managed KMS while we finish procurement.
- Caching: We will configure region-scoped in-memory KV caches with strict TTL and no persistent writes for the pilot; for production on Private we can eliminate cross-region caching entirely.
- Cross-region routing: Redwood's routing policies can be configured by account. We can set a strict "EU-only execution" policy which prevents failover to non-EU pools. That is not the default for all accounts, but it's a configuration we can enforce (and we will document it in the runbook).

For Thu 14 CET let's aim to:
1) Walk through the Dedicated trial plan and what we can provision in EU for benchmarking.
2) Rishi/Connor to run through latency/region matrix live and note any constraints.
3) Outline the split scope: pilot (Dedicated trial, Redwood-managed KMS) -> production (Private VPC with customer HSM).

Connor and Rishi — can you pull the EU latency baselines and the Dedicated cluster availability for the next 30 days and drop here before Thu? I've attached the deployment checklist for procurement to the thread.

Marissa

Attachments: deployment-checklist.docx

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sofie Larsen <sofie.larsen@nordbank.com>, Mikael Hansen <mikael.hansen@nordbank.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Jul 2026 14:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode & EU data residency — follow-up and next steps

Hi all — quick update ahead of Thu: attached is the EU region availability sheet (short list) and a one-page note on Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs. High-level: 

- EU Dedicated pools: Frankfurt (eu-central-1), Amsterdam (eu-west-1), and Paris (eu-west-3) currently support Dedicated nodes with latency baselines meeting your 150ms p95 target for standard LLM routing.
- Cross-region routing: can be disabled per-account. If you choose "EU-only execution" we will not route to non-EU pools even under burst. For very large bursts we recommend Dedicated with burst capacity pre-provisioned; Private VPC allows you to control autoscaling beyond that.
- KMS/HSM: HSM-backed customer KMS available for Private VPC only. For Dedicated we can integrate with your external KMS for key wrapping on a case-by-case basis (needs legal/engineering review).

Attachments included: eu-region-availability.xlsx, redwood-deployment-options.pdf

I'll be on the call Thu 14 CET and can run the latency baselines. If helpful I'll bring a short checklist of what procurement will need for the DPA/SOC2 evidence.

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference
